subject: Clarify IP infringement carve-out & Order Form liability language
messages:
From: Matt Reynolds <matt.reynolds@bluewave.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com; procurement@bluewave.com
Cc: sara.chen@bluewave.com
Date: 2027-10-06T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP indemnity (MSA redlines attached)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are the redlines our legal team has proposed to the Redwood MSA and the Order Form. High level request: BlueWave needs the liability cap to exclude amounts payable under IP infringement indemnity (we propose unlimited liability for third-party claims caused by Redwood’s Product), and we also want to preserve equitable relief (injunctive) and recovery for willful infringement without cap.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept an IP indemnity carve-out that removes the cap entirely for amounts finally adjudicated against Redwood? If not, please propose concrete alternative language (e.g., a carve-out limited to direct damages only, or a per-claim cap). We are under a compressed procurement timeline so appreciate a quick turnaround.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx (track changes), BlueWave_IP_Request.pdf (summary & commercial rationale)

—Matt
Matt Reynolds
Head of Procurement | BlueWave Systems

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-10-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP indemnity (MSA redlines attached)

Matt —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. Quick read: BlueWave’s proposed language removes the monetary cap for all IP indemnity payouts (including settlements), plus keeps injunctive relief and willful infringement outside the cap. Our concern is that an uncapped exposure is a material commercial change and we need alignment from finance and our executive sponsors.

Proposed middle-ground (suggested edits below):
- Carve-out scope: Agreement to carve IP indemnity obligations out of the general liability cap only to the extent of amounts expressly awarded in a final court judgment or agreed settlement arising from a claim that the Product as delivered infringes a third party’s patent, copyright or trademark.
- Damage type: Limit the carve-out to "direct monetary damages" (expressly exclude exemplary, punitive, consequential, indirect, and loss of business).
- Defense & control: Redwood will take primary control of the defense of any indemnified claim and will have the right to settle (with consent not to be unreasonably withheld). Customer must provide prompt written notice and cooperation.
- Willful infringement: If a final adjudication expressly finds willful infringement, then amounts awarded for willful infringement (but not punitive/exemplary damages) will be excluded from the liability cap.
- Insurance & mitigation: If BlueWave requires, Redwood will provide proof of commercial liability/tech E&O insurance covering IP risks up to $10M; parties can negotiate higher limits for larger deals.

If BlueWave cannot accept a carve-out limited to final adjudication for direct damages, please confirm that and indicate whether a per-claim monetary floor (e.g., $5M specific for IP indemnity claims) would be acceptable commercially.

I’m looping in Karthik (legal) and Marissa (contracts) to propose redline language. Will aim to get a defensible redline back by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Date: 2027-10-07T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP indemnity (MSA redlines attached)

Team —

Draft redline summary below (high level, please see attached suggested clause):
- "IP Indemnity Carve-Out": Notwithstanding any limitation of liability in this Agreement, amounts payable by Redwood under Sections [IP Indemnity] that are finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction (or paid in settlement with the Customer’s consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld) arising from a third-party claim that the Product as provided by Redwood infringes a third party’s intellectual property rights shall be excluded from the liability cap, but only to the extent of direct monetary damages.
- "Direct monetary damages" defined to exclude consequential, incidental, punitive, exemplary, and other non-direct categories.
- Customer obligations: Customer must (i) promptly notify Redwood in writing of any claim; (ii) allow Redwood to assume the defense and settlement negotiations; (iii) provide reasonable assistance and authority to settle.
- Willful infringement carve-out: If a final adjudication expressly finds willful infringement by Redwood, the carve-out will include amounts awarded for willful infringement; however, punitive/exemplary damages remain excluded from carve-out.
- Limited settlement escrow: For cases where settlement reasonably requires a holdback or escrow, parties agree to good faith discussions to set escrow amounts consistent with commerciality.

Rationale: This preserves a path for BlueWave to recover adjudicated IP losses while keeping broad uncapped exposure off the table. It also preserves Redwood’s control over defense and reduces risk of collusive settlements that inflate exposure.

Marissa — please attach the clause version for inclusion in the order form redline set. Matt/Sara — let us know if the requirement that carve-out attach only to "final adjudication or settlement with consent" is a dealbreaker.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP indemnity (MSA redlines attached)

Olga/Karthik —

Thanks for the thoughtful approach. BlueWave can accept a carve-out that is limited to direct monetary damages awarded in a final adjudication or in a settlement that the Customer reasonably approves. Two clarifications we need to preserve: (1) any settlement that would materially affect the Customer’s business (including amounts tied to a product recall or redesign) requires BlueWave’s consent (we will not unreasonably withhold); and (2) for willful infringement, while we accept Redwood’s proposal to exclude punitive/exemplary damages, we want explicit language that willful infringement awards (as part of a final adjudication) are not subject to the cap.

We are also agreeable to Redwood providing proof of E&O/IP endorsement with a $10M limit for this transaction; BlueWave will confirm if higher limits are needed after we complete our risk review.

Next steps: I will ask procurement to accept Redwood’s redline with the language Karthik proposed and mark up only the settlement consent carve-out (clarify the reasonableness standard). If that’s fine, can Redwood produce a clean MSA + Order Form that reflect this by COB Friday? We are trying to route for signature next week.

Appreciate the fast collaboration.

—Matt
Matt Reynolds
Head of Procurement | BlueWave Systems
